Bill.BriefDescription: Providing patients with information on options for breast reconstruction.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to providing patients with information on optionsfor breast reconstruction; adding a new section to chapter 70.41 RCW;and adding a new section to chapter 70.230 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 70.41 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) A hospital in which a mastectomy, lymph node dissection, orlumpectomy is performed shall provide the patient with informationregarding the option of postprocedure reconstructive surgery. Theinformation must be provided to the patient in writing and in advanceof obtaining consent to the procedure. (2) The information must include at least the following: (a) A description of the various reconstructive options and theadvantages and disadvantages of each; (b) A description of the statutory provisions requiring coverage byinsurers for reconstructive surgery following a mastectomy in 29 U.S.C.Sec. 1885b, RCW 48.20.395, 48.21.230, 48.44.330, and 48.46.280; (c) A description of how a patient may access reconstructive care, p. 1 HB 1101including the potential of transferring to another facility or choosingto pursue reconstruction after the completion of breast cancer surgeryand chemotherapy or radiotherapy, if warranted; and (d) Any other information as may be required by the department.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 70.230 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) An ambulatory surgical facility in which a mastectomy, lymphnode dissection, or lumpectomy is performed shall provide the patientwith information regarding the option of postprocedure reconstructivesurgery. The information must be provided to the patient in writingand in advance of obtaining consent to the procedure. (2) The information must include at least the following: (a) A description of the various reconstructive options and theadvantages and disadvantages of each; (b) A description of the statutory provisions requiring coverage byinsurers for reconstructive surgery following a mastectomy in 29 U.S.C.Sec. 1885b, RCW 48.20.395, 48.21.230, 48.44.330, and 48.46.280; (c) A description of how a patient may access reconstructive care,including the potential of transferring to another facility or choosingto pursue reconstruction after the completion of breast cancer surgeryand chemotherapy or radiotherapy, if warranted; and (d) Any other information as may be required by the department.
